title: Explicit expression and fast algorithms for the inverse of some matrices arising from implicit time integration

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The lemma states, for i≠j, that the sum equals ∏_{k≠j}(c_j-c_k). But in the proof, setting x=c_j makes all terms with m≠j vanish, leaving only ∏_{k≠i,j}(c_j-c_k). For n=1, i=0, j=1, the left side is 1 while the stated right side is c_1-c_0, which is generally not 1. The theorem's final formula uses the correct product excluding both i and j, so the lemma statement is internally inconsistent.

Equation (2.9) defines binom{c_n}{c_0} = (-1)^n ∏_{k=0}^{n-1}(c_n-c_k) / ∏_{k=0}^{n-1}(c_{n-k}-c_0). For c_i=i and n=1, this gives -1, not the binomial coefficient binom{1}{0}=1; for n=3 it gives -1 versus binom{3}{0}=1. Thus the claim that it reduces to the ordinary binomial coefficient is false, and Theorem 2.2's second equality gives the wrong sign for W_{0j} (or W_{i0}) when n is odd.

Equation (2.18) states H^T = F [ [0,c_0^T], [c_0,C_n] ]. For n=1, H^T=[[0,1],[0,0]], but the right-hand side with C_n=c_1 gives [[0,c_1],[0,0]]. The correct factor is D_n (with diagonal entries 1,...,n), as is actually used in the subsequent substitution in (2.19).

Algorithm 3.1 computes coefficients b_k of ψ(x)=∏_{k≠i}(x-c_k), then uses W_{ij}=(1/(c_j-c_i)) ψ(c_j)/ψ(c_i). For i≠j, ψ(c_j) contains the factor c_j-c_j=0, so this formula would make every off-diagonal entry zero, which is impossible. The numerator should be ψ_j(c_j)=∏_{k≠j}(c_j-c_k), not the same ψ associated with exclusion of i.

Algorithms 3.1–3.3 are stated for inputs satisfying c(0)<c(1)<...<c(n). However, Example 3 defines c_i = 1/2 + 1/2 cos((2i+1)π/(2n+1)), which is decreasing in i (c_0≈1 and c_n=0). The text does not say the nodes are reordered before use, so the experimental setup appears to violate the stated input precondition.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction claim about BIM inverse versus Section 2.2 BIM formula
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The introduction states that the inverse of the BIM matrix is exactly W_n^T when c_i=i. Section 2.2 then gives N = D_n(V_nD_nV_n^{-1}D_n^{-1})D_n^{-1}+D_n^{-1} and calls it the inverse of the BIM matrix. For n=1, W_n^T=1 but this formula gives N=2, so the two statements cannot both be correct as written.
